**Scope(s):** THEORY-LEVEL · **Row count:** 1 · **Lifecycle (candidate):** DORMANT · **Layer (provisional):** LAYER-UNRESOLVED
**Notations:** `C=<Proposition,Context,Scope,Time,Source>`, `Contradiction requires SemanticAlignment (compatible time, scope, version, interpretation)`, `eight-category conflict-candidate taxonomy: scope/time/version/interpretation/insufficient-evidence/genuine-contradiction/correction/supersession` · **Aliases:** `is it really a contradiction? alignment checks`

Ungrouped — no mechanical signal connected this label to any other in P2a.

## Sources (how this label entered the ledger)
- **OBJECT-INDEX** (batch B0033, scope THEORY-LEVEL): Step 181 requires establishing SemanticAlignment before declaring a genuine contradiction, checking time (FirewallOpen(t1) vs FirewallClosed(t2) may just mean the firewall changed), scope (FirewallOpen(Production) vs FirewallClosed(Test) concern different environments), version (Nexus supports X at v3.70 vs does not at v3.69 reflects evolution, not conflict), and interpretation (two engineers meaning different things by 'the migration is safe' -- no data loss vs no service interruption -- is semantic ambiguity, not contradiction, framed via DDD: words have meaning inside bounded contexts, e.g. 'safe' differs between SecurityContext and OperationsContext, so KnowledgeOS must not flatten organizational language into one premature universal ontology). Proposes a claim tuple C=<Proposition,Context,Scope,Time,Source> and an eight-category (experimental) conflict-candidate taxonomy: different scope, different time, different version, different interpretation, incomplete evidence, genuine contradiction, correction, supersession -- only genuine contradiction requires C1=P and C2=not-P under materially equivalent context/scope/time.
